title: Accounts Manager
description:
Account Manager Accountancy Practice

Location: Somerset (office-based across two local offices)
Job Type: Permanent Part-Time (up to 40 hours per week)
Salary: £35,000 £40,000 FTE (depending on experience)

A well-established and growing accountancy practice is looking to recruit an experienced Account Manager to join its friendly and supportive team.

This is a fantastic opportunity for an experienced practice accountant who enjoys working closely with a varied client portfolio and is looking for a role offering flexibility, autonomy, and long-term career stability.

The Role

You'll be responsible for managing a portfolio of clients, ensuring a high standard of service across accounts preparation, bookkeeping, VAT, payroll, and general compliance. This is a varied role where you'll build strong client relationships while supporting businesses with their day-to-day accounting requirements.

The successful candidate will have the flexibility to spread their hours across two local offices and should be comfortable travelling between sites when required.

Key Responsibilities
- Managing a portfolio of clients across a range of industries.
- Preparing management accounts, year-end accounts, and financial reports.
- Completing bookkeeping, bank reconciliations, and maintaining accurate accounting records.
- Preparing and submitting VAT returns in line with HMRC requirements.
- Supporting payroll processing where required.
- Managing accounts payable and receivable.
- Assisting with year-end compliance and liaising with senior colleagues where necessary.
- Building and maintaining strong client relationships, acting as a key point of contact.
- Supporting clients with accounting software and day-to-day finance queries.
- Ensuring compliance with accounting standards and HMRC regulations.
- Identifying opportunities to improve internal processes and client service.

About You

The ideal candidate will have:
- ACA, ACCA, CIMA or equivalent professional qualification.
- A minimum of three years' post-qualified experience within an accountancy practice.
- Experience preparing statutory accounts, VAT returns, payroll, self-assessment tax returns, and limited company accounts.
- Strong working knowledge of cloud accounting software such as Xero, QuickBooks, Sage, or similar.
- Excellent organisational skills with the ability to manage multiple deadlines.
- Strong communication and client relationship skills.
- A proactive and professional approach with excellent attention to detail.
- The ability to travel between two local office locations as required.

What's on Offer
- Salary of £35,000 £40,000 FTE, depending on experience.
- Flexible part-time hours (up to 40 hours per week).
- Friendly and supportive working environment.
- Health and wellbeing initiatives.
- Company events.
- Long-term opportunity within a respected and growing accountancy practice.

If you're an experienced practice accountant looking for a varied client-facing role with flexibility and genuine career stability, we'd love to hear from you.

title: P/T ACCOUNTS ADMINISTRATOR / BOOKKEEPER
description:
ACCOUNTS ADMINISTRATOR / BOOKKEEPER

Somerset Solders Ltd, incorporating Somerset Workwear, is an established and growing Somerset business supplying customers across the electronics, construction, medical and transport sectors. We are an accredited Real Living Wage Employer and a Supporter of the West of England Good Employment Charter

This role is based at our Radstock site, we re open to discussing flexible start and finish times, compressed hours or part-time working. Please talk to us about what works for you.

We are looking for an experienced and dependable Accounts Administrator to join our small, friendly team. This is a varied, hands-on role with responsibility for the day-to-day accounting administration of the business.

We are offering a permanent position working 16 hours per week with a flexible approach on how the hours are worked with hybrid working to be discussed.

Key responsibilities as a accounts administrator / bookkeeper :
- Maintaining sales and purchase ledgers
- Credit control and customer statements
- Bank and nominal ledger reconciliations
- Resolving supplier and customer invoice queries
- Preparing and submitting VAT returns, ensuring VAT is correctly accounted for on transactions
- Liaising with colleagues, customers and suppliers on accounts matters
- Supporting month-end accounting processes / reporting to management
- Supporting our waste reduction, recycling and responsible sourcing practices in your day-to-day work.

You ll ideally have at least two years experience in bookkeeping or a similar accounting role and be comfortable working independently across a range of day-to-day accounting tasks. Experience with Xero is essential. Previous experience in working with an ERP system will be an advantage.

We offer you as a accounts administrator / bookkeeper:

You ll receive a full induction, ongoing training during paid working hours, opportunities for further professional development and regular one-to-ones coupled with an annual appraisal to support your development.
- Permanent part-time position 16 hours per week
- £25,00-£30,000 pro rata
- Flexible working hours to be discussed
- Opportunity for some hybrid working once established in the role
- Salary based on experience
- Company pension
- Free on-site parking
- Friendly, supportive small-team environment
- Training on the company ERP system
- Holiday entitlement increases with length of service
- We close between Christmas and New Year, usually around a week
- 20% staff discount off our products

If you would like to join us, please apply by emailing your CV for the attention of Caira Day

We welcome applications from everyone, regardless of age, disability, ethnicity, gender, religion, sexual orientation or background, and we particularly encourage applications from groups under-represented in our industry. We welcome applications from service leavers, reservists and military spouses and partners. We shortlist on skills and experience. If you need any adjustments to the application or interview process, just let us know and we ll be happy to help

title: Payroll Officer
description:
Payroll Officer

Salary: 35,000 - 40,000 Location: North Somerset Hours: Full time or part time (22.5 hours minimum) considered

Are you an experienced payroll professional looking for a role where you can make a real impact?

Reed Payroll are delighted to be partnering with a well-established charity organisation in North Somerset to recruit a Payroll Officer. This is an excellent opportunity to join a values-driven organisation that provides vital services for the local community.

This role sits at the heart of both Finance and HR, offering much more variety than a traditional payroll position. Alongside taking ownership of payroll processing, you will have the opportunity to support payroll journals, reconciliations, pension administration and process improvement initiatives as the organisation continues to grow.

The organisation offers genuine flexibility and is focused on finding the right individual rather than fitting someone into a rigid working pattern.

The Role

As Payroll Officer, you will be responsible for delivering accurate and timely payroll services across weekly and monthly payroll cycles, while working closely with both Finance and HR colleagues.

Key responsibilities include:
- Processing weekly and monthly payrolls
- Managing payroll amendments including starters, leavers, salary changes and contractual updates
- Preparing payroll journals and reconciliations
- Administering workplace pension schemes and auto-enrolment processes
- Supporting salary sacrifice arrangements and employee benefits
- Maintaining accurate payroll records and ensuring compliance with payroll legislation
- Resolving payroll queries from employees and managers
- Producing payroll reports and supporting month-end processes
- Identifying opportunities to improve payroll processes, controls and efficiencies
- Working collaboratively with HR and Finance to ensure data accuracy and seamless payroll delivery
- This is a great opportunity for someone who enjoys problem-solving, improving processes and being involved in wider business operations.

About You

To be successful in this role, you will ideally have:
- Previous end-to-end payroll experience
- Experience preparing payroll journals and reconciliations
- Strong knowledge of UK payroll legislation and statutory payments
- Pension administration experience, including auto-enrolment
- Experience working with salary sacrifice schemes
- Strong Excel skills and confidence working with manual payroll processes
- Excellent attention to detail and organisational skills
- The ability to build strong working relationships across Finance and HR teams
- A proactive mindset with a continuous improvement approach
- Experience within the charity or not-for-profit sector would be advantageous but is by no means essential.

What's in it for You?
- Salary of 35,000 - 40,000 depending on experience
- Flexible working arrangements tailored around the successful candidate
- 28 days annual leave plus bank holidays (pro rata for part-time roles)
- Health Cash Plan
- Discounted gym membership
- Training and development opportunities
- Childcare discounts
- Employee assistance and counselling services
- Retail discount schemes
- The opportunity to join a friendly, supportive and purpose-driven organisation

If this sounds like the role for you, please apply online ASAP, successful applicants will be contacted within the next 24 working hours.

title: Service Controller

title: Bookkeeper
description:
Part-Time Bookkeeper

BakeryBits Wellington, Somerset 12 hours per week

A flexible opportunity for an experienced bookkeeper to join our team.

BakeryBits is looking for a reliable, organised and experienced Part-Time Bookkeeper to manage the day-to-day bookkeeping and financial administration of our business.

Working closely with our Commercial & Finance Manager, Managing Director and Operations Manager, you will play a key role in maintaining accurate financial records, managing payments and supporting monthly accounts and payroll.

The Role

Your responsibilities will include:
- Purchase Ledger: Checking supplier invoices against purchase orders and delivery records, investigating discrepancies, processing approved invoices in Xero, reconciling statements and preparing payments.
- Bookkeeping: Maintaining accurate Xero records, completing bank and credit card reconciliations, processing expenses and routine journals, and keeping electronic records organised.
- Sales Ledger & Credit Control: Monitoring customer accounts, chasing overdue invoices, reconciling balances and escalating payment issues.
- Month-End & VAT: Preparing prepayments and accruals, completing balance sheet reconciliations, supporting management accounts and preparing VAT returns in Xero for review.
- Payroll & Pensions: Running monthly payroll for approximately nine employees using SafeHR, processing occasional starters and leavers, managing pension information and handling routine payroll queries.

About You

You will be confident managing the finances of a small business, able to work independently and have excellent attention to detail.

Essential experience and skills:
- Practical bookkeeping experience within an SME.
- Confident working knowledge of Xero.
- Experience with purchase and sales ledgers, invoice matching and credit control.
- Understanding of prepayments, accruals, reconciliations and month-end procedures.
- Good Excel skills and strong organisational abilities.
- Ability to work independently and meet deadlines.

Desirable:
- AAT qualification or qualified by experience (QBE).
- Experience in a product-based, wholesale or stock-related business.
- Familiarity with SafeHR or similar payroll systems.

Working Arrangements
- Hours: 12 hours per week, with flexibility around scheduling.
- Location: Wellington, Somerset, or surrounding area.
- On-site: Minimum attendance once every two weeks.
- Salary: Dependent on experience.

We have two posts available which will require flexibility within working hours as well as location across our three surgeries at St Chads, Somerton House and Chilcompton. Come and join our team to make a real difference in your community! Key Responsibilities: Be the welcoming face of our practice, greeting and checking in patients. Coordinate with doctors and staff to keep appointments running smoothly. Maintain patient records and manage appointments with precision and care. Support with vital admin tasks. Ready to make an impact? Join us and be part of a team that makes a difference every day The duties and responsibilities to be undertaken by members of the reception team may include any or all of the items listed below. Duties may be varied from time to time under the direction of the lead receptionist or member of the management team dependent on current and evolving practice workload and staffing levels: Processing face to face and telephone enquiries and requests for appointments, visits, and telephone consultation, ensuring callers are directed to the appropriate healthcare professional or management or other department as appropriate. Initiating contact with and responding to requests from patients, other team members and outside agencies. Exercise care and proper use of telephones and computer systems in normal daily working, maintaining and updating patient information in the practice appointment system. Processing personal and medical information from the patient in accordance with practice protocols, maintaining confidentiality and recording information appropriately within the clinical systems, such as triage requests, messages, updates on health status, medical information on appointments etc. Opening up/locking up of the practice premises and maintaining security in accordance with practice protocols. Checks patients and visitors in when they arrive at the surgery for appointments Assist patients in the use of the self-check in screen and encourages the increased use of this method of checking in, as appropriate Pass on urgent information to doctors, nurses and other surgery staff members and also back to patients in an appropriate way Providing adhoc clerical assistance to other members of the practice team from time to time including using IT software such as Microsoft Word or finding or filing physical documents or patient files.. Handling and storing patient samples brought in at the reception desk in an appropriate way maintaining infection control standards and making sure the samples are suitably labelled with the patients details before the patient leaves. Keeping own work space, the reception area, waiting room, noticeboards and leaflet dispensers tidy and free from obstruction and clutter. Attend and participate in any team or whole practice meetings when required. These may be on days you do not normally work, however you will be at times expected to attend and overtime will be paid. Notice for such meetings will be given in advance. Other duties as requested from time to time.

title: Senior Administrator
description: An exciting opportunity has arisen to join the Children and Young People's Therapy Service as a Band 3 Administrator. Working as part of a friendly and supportive multidisciplinary team, you will provide high-quality administrative and secretarial support to managers and therapy staff, helping to ensure children, young people and their families receive an efficient and responsive service. The service delivers Physiotherapy, Occupational Therapy and Speech and Language Therapy across Somerset, working closely with children, young people, families and partner agencies to support positive outcomes and achieve individual goals. The team member will also provide flexible administrative support to the Podiatry booking office as required and requested by the Administration Manager to support service requirements. As a key member of the team, you will be the first point of contact for patients, families, staff and external organisations, managing enquiries professionally and sensitively. You will support appointment systems, maintain accurate records, process referrals, coordinate administrative activities and contribute to the smooth day-to-day running of the service. This role would suit an organised and customer-focused administrator with excellent communication skills, attention to detail and the ability to manage a varied workload in a busy healthcare environment. Act as a first point of contact for patients, families, staff and external agencies, responding to enquiries by telephone, email and in person. Provide comprehensive administrative and secretarial support to managers and therapy staff across the Children and Young People's Therapy Service. Support patient appointment booking systems and clinic administration. Maintain accurate electronic and paper records using a range of IT systems and databases. Input data and update information systems to support service delivery, reporting and audit requirements. Produce correspondence, reports and other documentation to a high standard while maintaining confidentiality. Assist with referral and triage administration processes within the service. Prioritise workload effectively, ensuring deadlines and service requirements are met. Support reception services and provide a welcoming experience for patients and visitors. Maintain office supplies, equipment and filing systems, contributing to the efficient operation of the department. The Children and Young People's Therapy Service provides Physiotherapy, Occupational Therapy and Speech and Language Therapy for children and young people across Somerset. The successful post holder will play a vital role in supporting the delivery of these services through the provision of effective and professional administrative support. Key responsibilities include: Communication and Customer Service Providing a professional and welcoming first point of contact for the service. Greeting patients and visitors and assisting with enquiries. Responding to telephone calls promptly, taking accurate messages and ensuring information is shared with the appropriate team members. Communicating sensitively and professionally with families, colleagues and partner agencies. Managing confidential and sensitive information in accordance with Trust policies and data protection requirements. Administration and Information Management Providing administrative support to managers, therapists and therapy support staff. Managing appointment and clinic administration processes. Producing letters, reports and other documentation accurately and efficiently. Maintaining electronic and paper-based filing systems. Processing incoming and outgoing correspondence and deliveries. Using a range of IT systems including email, Microsoft Office applications and patient record systems to maintain accurate records and support service delivery. Planning and Organisational Support Prioritising and managing a varied workload with minimal supervision. Supporting the organisation of training events and meetings where required. Operating reminder and follow-up systems to ensure actions are completed within required timescales. Supporting the single point of access and triage processes for the service. Data and Reporting Recording and maintaining accurate information on service databases and information systems. Supporting data collection, audits and reporting activities as requested by managers. Assisting the team in providing accurate service information and performance data. General Responsibilities Supporting the security of confidential information and office equipment. Assisting with the maintenance of office resources and stock levels. Participating in mandatory training and continuous professional development. Working in accordance with Trust values of Kindness, Respect and Teamwork. Supporting safeguarding, confidentiality, equality and diversity, health and safety, and information governance requirements.
